noise.best_discriminator: med and gpuMs on fixed-renderScale rows (cost questions). For holds-60 verdicts use p95gb2, never p95gb: the same row's p95gb ranged 4.5 ms across reports (high@rd=8 12.7-17.2) and p95gb2 removes most of it (ultra@rd=8 p95gb 18.5 -> p95gb2 12.3). Auto rows add governor noise: med moves 0.6-0.7 ms when the governor lands at 1.0 instead of 0.9 (bench-sh5-v7 medium vs bench-sh5-medium).
noise.seconds_effect: From per-frame data (bench-lab2-raw1.json, rd 12), 4-s windows already give med SD <= 0.2 and gpu SD <= 0.15 within a run, below the 0.2-0.34 pass-to-pass SD. Longer windows only tame the p95 tail, which is bursty (one 2-s window of high@1 read p95gb2 24.6 vs 16-17).
noise.verdict_flips: 5 of 74 single passes (rd 12, 3-pass reports) gave another holds-60 verdict than their row's median: all on p95, never on med. Their combined p95gb margins were -0.75, +2.74, -0.30, +1.02, +1.12 ms.
noise.note: _pct = one-pass SD relative to a typical preset row (med ~12, gpu ~13, p95gb2 ~15). A delta below 2 SD (real_delta_ms) is noise.

thermal.signature: No GPU-thermal throttling was seen: over ~5 h of near-continuous GPU load on 11-03, vanilla stayed at 4.4-5.0 ms med with no trend. Every flagged or slow pass was background CPU load: sysCpuPct >= 58 (lead's govsim, SwiftShader smokes, 83% in bench-sh2-a-final). --cooldown 60 did not prevent it (bench-final-1.5 and -native pass 1 were both flagged). With cooldown 0, bench-sh5-medium crept +0.3 ms (vanilla 4.6/4.8/4.9).
thermal.detect_early: Preflight: vanilla med > 5.0 or p95gb > 8.5 or sysCpuPct > 55 = bad state. Per row: sysCpuPct > 50 on a heavy row (normal 33-48) = suspect, even when vanilla looks fine.
thermal.why_cooldown: 30 s is cheap insurance against the +0.3 ms creep. The data shows no benefit from 60 s.

wall_time.warp_check: reports/bench-devloop-warp-ab.json (warp 10, settle 12, 5 s, interleaved): vanilla warped 4.75 (gpu 4.75) vs legacy 4.5 (4.47); high 11.9 (12.40) vs 12.0 (12.35); every row at clock 40.0-40.1. All deltas within 1-pass noise, so warped rows are comparable with --at 40 reports; no separate vanilla range needed
wall_time.model: per scenario ~ at + seconds + 3-5 s (boot, steady and warm-up overlap the camera wait); total ~ scenarios x passes x 52 s + passes x cooldown + ~10 s browser start
wall_time.where_it_goes: About 75% of each scenario is the wait for the title camera to reach --at 40 s of game time. --seconds 8 -> 5 saves only ~3 s (6%). Runs at --at 20 took 29-32 s per scenario, and at --at ~8 they took 15-17 s, but that is another view (vanilla 3.9-4.2 vs 4.7). A steady wait longer than ~35 s pushes a row past 53 s: angle-gl high took 81 s.

screen.why: For A/B cost questions on med/gpuMs. 4-5 s windows give med/gpu SD <= 0.2, so a 1-pass Δ above 0.6 ms med or 0.9 ms GPU is real (same run). Keep fixed renderScale on the rows being compared (Auto adds 0.6-0.7 ms governor noise). Never judge holds-60 from a screen run.

accept.adaptive: After pass 1, a row's verdict is settled when |p95gb2 - 16.7| >= 2.0 and |med - 14| >= 0.8. Rows inside those margins need passes 2-3. Under vsync: settled when miss% < 0.5 or > 1.5; otherwise rerun at 60 s.
accept.why: 3 passes because 5/74 single passes flipped the p95 verdict and Auto p95gb moved 1.2-2.6 ms between a 1-pass and a 3-pass run of the same build. Vsync needs >= 30 s: at 8 s one frame is 0.21 pp of miss% (bench-bench4-vsync-check failed by 0.05 pp), at 30 s it is 0.056 pp. SH5 used 40-s rows. The guard can't see throttling under vsync, so run it uncapped first.

first_guess.hold 60 at the standard (uncapped): high (Auto). 11.0 / p95gb2 14.45 at scale 0.85 has the widest margin of the enabled presets (bench-sh5-v7); low (13.73) if Auto must stay at 1.0. Accept with --protocol accept.
first_guess.max quality that holds 60 under vsync: ultra (Auto): SH5's v7 40-s traces read miss 0.17% at scale 0.994 with 3 changes/min, and ultra-moving 0.59%. Confirm with --vsync --seconds 30 --repeat 2 on vanilla,ultra,ultra-moving (~8.5 min).
first_guess.cheapest shadows: medium, or high+shadowCascades=false. Turning shadows on costs ~2 GPU ms at rd 12 (1.6 at rd 8). Every shadow knob (filter 0/1/2, cascades, size 1024-2048) is within 0.7 ms = noise; only shadowSize=4096 costs (+2.1 GPU, p95gb +11). Cascades off halves redraws (30 -> 15/min). For a real saving use renderScale (0.9: ~-1.3 ms on medium; 0.7: -2 to -3 ms) or shadows off.
first_guess.is my GLSL change a per-primitive regres: Compare off vs vanilla at rd 12 and rd 8: today's off tax is +0.1-0.4 GPU ms at rd 12. More than ~1 ms at rd 12, growing with rd, means a geometry-shader-style per-primitive cost such as a flat varying (+3.0 at rd 12, +1.1 at rd 8).
first_guess.rd 8 player: high or ultra at scale 1: 10.2-10.8 med, p95gb2 12.3 (bench-sh5-secondary).
first_guess.worst-case secondary row: high@rd=10 (12.1 / 15.5) and high@fov=110 (16.4, 0.3 from the line). FOV 110 is cheaper than FOV 80 for the script at scale 1; FOV 70 is dearer.
